source.section: PDF page 23, Table E (Single, more than 15,000 to 18,800: .75) and Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 7-10; PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 18,000.00 = 18,000.00. Federal taxable income = 18,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 2,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 18,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 18,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 0.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 0.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 18,000.00 - 0.00 = 18,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 18,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 18,000.00 is not more than 30,000.00, exemption 15,000.00; Line 3 taxable income = 18,000.00 - 15,000.00 = 3,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 3,000.00: 3,000.00 x 0.02 = 60.00 = 60.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 18,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 60.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.75 (Connecticut AGI 18,000.00 is in the band more than 15,000.00); Line 9 = 60.00 x 0.75 = 45.00. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 60.00 - 45.00 = 15.00 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Connecticut AGI 18,000 is under 18,800, where the Table E decimal first drops below .75.
